security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel code running in S-mode directly accesses a CSR whose address has csr[9:8] == 0b10 (hypervisor-level CSR) without first checking for H-extension presence or delegating through the hypervisor interface, causing an illegal-instruction trap that the kernel does not expect or handle at that point.
security_spec.summary: FreeBSD S-mode kernel code that directly accesses hypervisor CSRs (addr[9:8]=0b10) without H-extension mediation causes unexpected illegal-instruction traps, since the kernel can't distinguish a missing H-extension from a true violation at runtime without explicit probing

findings.finding: H-extension gate check: returns ENXIO before any hypervisor CSR can be accessed if has_hyp is false. This guards all subsequent vmmops_* callbacks against executing on hardware without the H-extension.

All hypervisor CSRs (hgatp, henvcfg, hie, hcounteren) are written only within the VMM run loop, which is reachable exclusively after vmmops_modinit() has verified has_hyp. The CPU is executing in HS-mode at this point (it entered via vmm_switch's sret to guest context), so these CSR accesses are architecturally valid.
All virtual supervisor CSRs (vsstatus, vsie, vstvec, vsscratch, vsepc, vscause, vstval, vsatp) and hvip are written only during VMM guest restore. Reachable only after the has_hyp gate has passed.
All virtual supervisor CSRs (vsstatus, vsie, vstvec, vsscratch, vsepc, vscause, vstval, vsatp) and hvip are read only during VMM guest save. Reachable only after the has_hyp gate has passed.
hedeleg and hideleg CSRs are configured to delegate exceptions/interrupts from HS-mode to VS-mode. Called from vmmops_run only, after the has_hyp gate.

hstatus CSR is swapped to enter guest context for hlvx.hu unprivileged loads. Called only from riscv_gen_inst_emul_data within vmmops_run's world-switch path. The old hstatus is saved and restored, and the CPU is in HS-mode at the point of access.
findings.snippet:
old_hstatus = csr_swap(hstatus, hypctx->guest_regs.hyp_hstatus);
old_stvec = csr_swap(stvec, entry);

findings.finding: htval and htinst are read on VM exit to capture hypervisor trap information. These CSRs are architecturally valid to read when executing in HS-mode after a guest trap, and are only accessed within the vmmops_run path.

hstatus CSR is atomically swapped during world-switch entry to transition to guest context. The host hstatus is saved to hypctx and the guest hstatus is loaded. The CPU running this code is already executing in HS-mode (entered from the C caller vmmops_run).
findings.snippet:
csrrw  t1, hstatus, t1
csrrw  t2, scounteren, t2
csrrw  t3, sscratch, a0
csrrw  t4, stvec, t4
csrw   sepc, t5

findings.finding: hstatus CSR is restored on world-switch return from guest back to host. The saved host hstatus (stored at vmm_switch entry) is atomically swapped back.
findings.snippet:
ld     t4, (HYP_H_HSTATUS)(a0)
csrrw  t4, hstatus, t4
csrrw  t5, sstatus, t5
sd     t0, (HYP_G_SEPC)(a0)
sd     t4, (HYP_G_HSTATUS)(a0)

findings.finding: htval and htinst are read in the unprivileged-load trap handler. This trap handler is only installed (via stvec) during hlvx.hu execution in riscv_unpriv_read(), which runs within the vmmops_run path after the has_hyp gate.
findings.snippet:
csrr   a1, htval
sd     a1, HYP_TRAP_HTVAL(a0)
csrr   a1, htinst
sd     a1, HYP_TRAP_HTINST(a0)

findings.finding: mcounteren is declared via DECLARE_CSR but never read or written anywhere in the kernel code. No risk of illegal access.
